lesson-philippine-constitution-accountab.quote: > Do not assume that a high-ranking title automatically makes an officer impeachable.
lesson-philippine-constitution-accountab.note: The required General Information Traps section is now present; Speed Tricks is optional under the supplied ruling.

lesson-philippine-constitution-accountab.quote: An impeachable officer is accused only of "inefficiency." Is inefficiency by itself one of the six named constitutional grounds for impeachment?
lesson-philippine-constitution-accountab.note: The rewrite now includes both a direct President eligibility case and a distinct case where inefficiency is outside the closed list.

lesson-philippine-constitution-accountab.quote: Article XI, Section $2$ also gives a closed list of impeachment grounds:
lesson-philippine-constitution-accountab.note: The grounds section number is now written as inline math, Section $2$.

lesson-philippine-constitution-accountab.quote: Being on the list only means that the accusation uses an allowed ground. It does not prove that the facts are true, that the case is legally sufficient, or that the officer must be convicted or removed.

general-information-philippine-constitut.quote: A culpable constitutional violation is a willful or intentional breach of the Constitution, not merely an honest mistake.
general-information-philippine-constitut.note: The rewrite now explains the culpability distinction and also applies it in a worked example.

general-information-philippine-constitut.quote: Treason involves betrayal of the country in the ways defined by criminal law, such as levying war against the Philippines or giving aid or comfort to its enemies.
general-information-philippine-constitut.note: The rewrite now gives a plain meaning and concrete conduct examples for treason.

general-information-philippine-constitut.quote: Bribery involves an improper benefit tied to an official act.
general-information-philippine-constitut.note: The rewrite now explains bribery and applies it to money exchanged for an official act.

general-information-philippine-constitut.quote: Graft and corruption cover serious misuse of public office for improper benefit. Using public power to steer an improper benefit to oneself can raise a graft or corruption issue.
general-information-philippine-constitut.note: The rewrite now explains the graft/corruption idea and gives a conduct pattern rather than only naming the ground.

general-information-philippine-constitut.quote: "Other high crimes" is a broad impeachment ground. The Constitution does not give a complete list of acts under it.
general-information-philippine-constitut.note: The rewrite now states the scope limitation instead of leaving other high crimes as a bare label.

general-information-philippine-constitut.quote: "Betrayal of public trust" is also broad. It can cover serious abuse, neglect, favoritism, or other conduct that makes a high officer unfit to keep a public trust.
general-information-philippine-constitut.note: The rewrite now gives conduct that can be classified under betrayal of public trust and later works a favoritism example.

general-information-philippine-constitut.quote: The House of Representatives has the exclusive power to initiate impeachment cases. A verified complaint may come from a House Member, or from a citizen if a House Member endorses it.
general-information-philippine-constitut.note: The rewrite now teaches initiation, House thresholds, Senate trial and conviction, presidential-trial presiding, judgment, and the one-year limit.

general-information-philippine-constitut.quote: The Ombudsman receives complaints against public officials and employees. The office may also investigate on its own when an official act or failure to act appears illegal, unjust, improper, or inefficient.
general-information-philippine-constitut.note: The rewrite now teaches complaint handling, investigation, corrective directions, recommended sanctions, records requests, and systemic recommendations.
